== DESIGN (operator ruling 2026-08-23: tier by impact/stability, select by what changed) ==

TIER 1 — pre-commit (fast, deterministic, host-insensitive; in tools/hooks/pre-commit, gate 3, after the claimlint floor + staged-path gates):
- tools/smoke.sh (measured 1s, T788) always runs.
- Fast pool (measured 2026-08-23 under load 6-8, upper bounds, all rc=0): regression-claimlint-output 2s, c7-json 1s, c7-scope 1s, promotion 1s, volatile 2s, orient 1s, directive-id-uniqueness 1s, directive-integrity 1s, managent-models 1s, managent-landmark 14s, suite-surfaces 6s, canonicalizer-parity 1s. Total ~33s under load, ~15-25s quiet; measured full-hook runs: 34s, 34s, 34s, 40s, 42s, 2s(selection), 4s(selection).
- Budget: FAST_BUDGET_WALL_SECS=45 stated in the hook, per-script cap PER_SCRIPT_WALL_SECS=60 via tools/runner (the project's only reliable time backstop on macOS). Budget exceedance WARNS loudly, does not refuse (tests that passed must not block a commit because the host is busy — observed on the 2026-08-23 verification run under load 8 + a concurrent unguarded suite); the budget is the design-time cap on pool additions and the warning is the drift census.
- Change-based selection (operator ruling): each test declares which modules it covers in the T790 module contract (docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S09-module-test-contract/spec.md); the hook computes the changed set from the staged diff; the union of covering arms runs. Rule (a): a test with no declared coverage always runs (smoke.sh — unknown coverage is not empty coverage). Rule (b): selection is additive to the periodic full run — the nightly catches selector bugs. The hook reads lines of the form `test <path> covers <module> [<module>...]` (TEST_GATE_CONTRACT env override for controls). Interface note: T790's spec (written today by claude-sonnet-5) declares coverage semantically by arm-ID prefix (S09-RUNNER-* etc.) and says the selector 'reads its coverage declaration from exactly this document' — it does NOT yet emit the `test <path> covers` lines this hook parses. Until it does, the hook falls back to rule (a) (full pool every commit) — safe, just slower. The handshake is a follow-up: the S09 implementation pass should emit machine lines in the format above, or the hook's reader must be extended to the spec's actual structure. NOT a blocker: with no parseable contract the gate still runs the whole fast pool, which is the correct conservative default.
- Bypass: TEST_GATE_BYPASS=<reason> — an EMPTY reason is REFUSED; a reasoned bypass is allowed and APPENDED to untracked/log/precommit-test-gate-bypass.log (timestamp, task id, HEAD, reason). git commit --no-verify cannot be intercepted from a pre-commit hook — the reasoned channel exists so the responsible path is available. Precedent: git-commit-mine --explicit.
- Surface: the hook prints the nightly/scheduled suite verdict (suite-truth.sh --read-result) on every commit — a red is visible without being asked; a stale green reads as UNKNOWN; a red is non-blocking for unrelated commits (a red suite blocks a consolidation pass, not unrelated work).
- State-dependent checks quarantined from the pool (T788): regression-argus-doctor (T442), regression-managent-integrity + regression-git-commit-mine (deploy-hygiene) live in the full-suite tier where their state is measured.
- Fixture-environment handling: the hook's test gate SKIPS in scratch repos (no build.zig — the regression-precommit.sh / regression-git-commit-mine-hook.sh arms), so the pre-existing hook-testing regression scripts keep working (verified: regression-precommit.sh ALL CONTROLS PASSED with the new hook, 2026-08-23).

TIER 2 — pre-consolidation (full suite, blocking): `sh tools/suite-truth.sh` must exit 0 before any pass of S06/S08 lands. Measured wall 906s (T788 baseline, quiet host); budget = the runner's 7200s --max-wall ceiling, stated in the script header. Null control demonstrated offline against the T788 quiet-host log (untracked/log/T788-suite.log): observed == manifest, cosmetic 0, evidence 26/26, exit 0.

TIER 3 — scheduled (nightly, quiet host, unattended): suite-truth.sh --scheduled — preflight refuses when a local model is resident (ollama ps non-empty or an mlx-engine runner — the 2026-08-08 load-contamination rule), when a fleet lane is in flight (any tools/runner process), or when another run holds the lock (untracked/test-gate/suite-truth.lock, single-instance). TEST_GATE_FORCE=1 bypasses preflight for controls. Writes its verdict to untracked/test-gate/last-result.json (where the hook reads it); expected wall 906s — a run that doubles it is itself a loud signal; a result older than its interval reads as UNKNOWN, never green (--read-result, --interval-hours, default 26h). == GATE-CLASSIFICATION FIX (T788 finding, owned by T789) ==
- crashed modules (terminated with signal) and failed (assertion) modules are extracted separately and both feed the module-level RED comparison, reported apart (the old single regex called assertion failures 'crashed').
- the Build Summary's `tests passed (N skipped, K failed)` form is parsed (the old regex only read `K crashed` and silently returned empty — the COUNT comparison was vacuous). tests-crashed stays gated; tests-failed is reported loudly.
- the CONSOLE cosmetic calc subtracts failed steps as well as crashed ones (T788: the main module's 3 failed tests were counted as cosmetic).
- the failed/crashed step count reads the Build Summary RECAP block only (after the 'Build Summary:' line) — the tree appears twice (inline + recap) and counting both double-counts every failed step and HIDES cosmetic noise (found on the verification run: FAILED_STEPS=2 for one failed step).
- KNOWN_NOISE registry: registered stderr leaks from passing test binaries are counted as debt (loud report, ratchet down). First entry: vb_mutants-M1-M10-leak (marker '[EXPECTED] M1-', owner T531/T564-class/evidence.print, review 2026-09-15) — src/vb_mutants.zig prints [EXPECTED] M1-M10 via std.debug.print; the fix (routing through evidence.print) is engine territory, out of T789's commit scope. Subtraction applies to every log; the ratchet (a marker that stops appearing must be struck — a fixed leak must ratchet the registry down) applies to real runs only, so synthetic --log controls never trip it.

== WHAT THIS GATE WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS WEEK, AND WHAT IT WOULD STILL MISS (the honest paragraph) ==
This week's whole story was T711's host-guard control: green the day it was written, never re-run, dead the day the fleet needed it. This gate catches that class by construction — the host-guard controls live in regression-runner-host-guard.sh, which the nightly (tier 3) now re-runs every day on a quiet host, so a control that rots stops being discovered by a fleet outage and starts being discovered by the machine within 24 hours; and the pre-commit tier re-runs smoke + the twelve core claimlint/orient/directive/managent/selection regressions on EVERY commit, so the deploy-staleness and hook-regression classes are caught at the commit that causes them. It would still miss: (a) anything the nightly refuses to run — if the host is never quiet (lanes always live, models resident), the scheduled tier refuses and the surface honestly reads UNKNOWN, but the verification simply does not happen; (b) state-dependent and deploy-hygiene checks in the full-suite tier, which only redden when their state is measured; (c) the evidence artifact when the run's env is misconfigured (my own WEIZIGO_EVIDENCE export bug this task — the gate reports '0/26 readings', which is loud, but only if someone reads the comparison); (d) anything --no-verify (uninspectable from a pre-commit hook); and (e) a module with no test at all — the pool + suite only re-run what exists (13 of 38 modules still have no regression script naming them; T790/S09 owns that census). The gate is additive: a selector bug, an env bug, a too-busy host — each fails LOUD (RED result, UNKNOWN staleness, refused preflight) rather than silently green, which is the T711 defect class and the bar.
